thread.title: Stocks Open Lower: Oil Bolsters Dow Jones, S&P 500 | Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Open Lower: Oil Bolsters Dow Jones, S&P 500 | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Stocks opened lower, then reversed to early gains Friday, after November jobs data, and as surging oil prices bolstered trade on the Dow and the S&P 500.
X Chipmaker Broadcom ( AVGO ) climbed after reporting fiscal fourth-quarter earnings . Lululemon Athletica ( LULU ), Big Lots ( BIG ) and Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ) fell hard after their reports. Marijuana stock Cronos Group ( CRON ) soared as Altria Group ( MO ) took a stake in the company. Tesla ( TSLA ) cleared a buy point after an analyst upgrade . Yelp ( YELP ) bolted higher on news that it would be added to the S&P MidCap 400 index.
The Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 each dipped 0.1%, then turned and ran up 0.5% and 0.4%, respectively. Dow Jones stock Exxon Mobil ( XOM ) leapt 2.4%, Chevron ( CVX ) jumped 2% in opening trade. Oil-related names notched 13 of the 15 top moves among S&P 500 stocks.
The Nasdaq Composite opened down 0.3%, then battled to a 0.2% gain. The four FANG stocks shed early losses and gained ground. Apple ( AAPL ) slipped 0.5%. Broadcom and Tesla were strongest, and Ulta Beauty was the weakest, among early movers on both the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Manufacturing Jobs Surge, Oil Prices Spike On OPEC U.S. non-farm employers hired 155,000 new workers in November , the Labor Department reported. That disappointed economists, who had expected a decline from October's 250,000 new hires, but only to 190,000 workers. The unemployment rate remained unchanged at 3.7%, as expected. Manufacturing jobs surged by 27,000, well above forecasts for a 16,000-worker increase. Growth in average hourly earnings was steady at 3.1%, just below projections for an uptick to 3.2%.
Oil prices jumped more than 4% as the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and non-OPEC allies led by Russia agreed to a 1.2 million barrel per day reduction in oil production. OPEC was reportedly set to handle 800,000 of the cutback, while Russia would shoulder 200,000 and other non-OPEC parters would trim another 200,000 bpd of output.
West Texas Intermediate reversed its early losses and vaulted nearly 5%, to near $54 a barrel. Brent crude popped 5.3% to trade above $63.
December consumer sentiment and BakerHughes ' ( BHGE ) weekly rig count survey are due out at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. ET, respectively.
Dow Jones Vs. 25,000; Small Caps Skirt Bear Territory In a week during which trading paused on Wednesday to pay tribute to former President George H.W. Bush, the Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 were both down 2.3% through Thursday. Some furious backtracking late Thursday left the Dow just below its 200-day moving average, as well as the 25,000 mark. It ended Thursday's session down 7.4% from its Oct. 3 high.
The Nasdaq fell 1.9% for the week through Thursday. Both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 ended well below the 50- and 200-day lines that have acted as clear levels of resistance in recent trade. The Nasdaq tried and failed to break that resistance on Nov. 7-8, and on Monday and Tuesday this week. The index ended Thursday 11.6% below its August high. But it is holding above its recent lows, and above the 7,000 level — both positives which have helped keep the current uptrend intact.
Small caps have undergone a much steeper consolidation. Two of the leading small-cap gauges, the Russell 2000 and S&P Smallcap 600, both undercut recent lows on Thursday. Both indexes backtracked to end above their prior low. The S&P 600's early dip stopped just short of the 20% border of bear-market territory. It ended the session 16.2% below its August high. The Russell ended Thursday 15.2% off its August high mark. These will be gauges to watch, to see whether that undercut marked a shakeout that could set the stage for a rebound, or whether it prefaced a breakdown that will deepen the consolidation.
Stocks: Tesla Breaks Out, Cronos Spikes Dow Jones stock Boeing edged 0.7% higher, in a make-or-break week for the stock's chart pattern. Shares ended Thursday down 4.3% after a high-volume attempt to retake the stock's 50-day moving average on Monday failed. The loss left shares a bit less than 11% above a Nov. 20 low, and damaged the stock's base-building effort.
Toronto-based Cronos Group catapulted 31% higher after confirming that tobacco maker Altria had paid $1.8 billion to take a 45% equity stake in the company. The agreement includes options that could raise Altria's holdings to 55% within four years, and allows Altria to nominate four directors to Cronos board. Altria Chairman and Chief Executive Howard Willard said Cronos would act as Altria's "exclusive partner in the global cannabis category." Altria shares rose 1.9%.
Yelp soared 3.4%, after Standard & Poor's announced late Thursday the stock would replace Gulfport Energy ( GPOR ) as a component on the S&P MidCap 400 Index. Gulfport will become an S&P Smallcap 600 component, replacing Oclaro ( OCLR ), which is being acquired by Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ). The changes will take effect on Dec. 12.
Yelp shares are in a deep, three-month consolidation, recovering from a harsh sell-off at the start of November.
Tesla climbed 3.7% gain, rising after Jefferies upgraded the stock to buy, from hold. The note hoisted the stock's price target to 450, from 360. The gain sent the stock above a 366.85 buy point in a cup-with-handle base. Shares remained in a buy range.
IBD 50 and Leaderboard stock Lululemon Athletica dropped 2.7%. The Vancouver, British Columbia-based company reported a 34% earnings gain over a 21% rise in revenue for its third quarter. Both numbers were above analyst targets. Management's revenue guidance apparently left some uncertainty among investors. The stock is shaping a possible base pattern, but must first deal with a trend of resistance at its 10-week moving average.
Hong Kong Holds Support; Germany Looks Beyond Merkel China's markets sent no clear signals Friday. A narrowly mixed day of trade left the Shanghai Composite a fraction higher and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index with a 0.4% loss. Shanghai ended the week up 0.7%. Hong Kong dropped 1.7%, but very narrowly held support at its 50-day moving average.
Markets in Europe continued to gain strength in afternoon trade as Germany's Christian Democratic Party met in Hamburg to appoint a new party head to succeed Chancellor Angela Merkel. The CAC-40 in Paris and London's FTSE 100 had gained 1.9% and 2.2%, respectively. Frankfurt's DAX was up 1%.
